        "originalContents": "\n\nconst PublicResumePage: React.FC\u003cPublicResumePageProps\u003e = () =\u003e {\n  const { uid } = useParams\u003c{ uid: string }\u003e();\n  const { t } = useTranslation();\n  const [profile, setProfile] = useState\u003cCrewProfile | null\u003e(null);\n  const [status, setStatus] = useState\u003cLoadingState\u003e(LOADING_STATES.LOADING);\n  const [error, setError] = useState\u003cstring | null\u003e(null);\n\n  useEffect(() =\u003e {\n    const fetchResume = async () =\u003e {\n      if (!uid) {\n        setStatus(LOADING_STATES.ERROR);\n        setError('No user ID provided');\n        return;\n      }\n\n      try {\n        setStatus(LOADING_STATES.LOADING);\n        const docRef = doc(db, 'crewProfiles', uid);\n        const docSnap = await getDoc(docRef);\n\n        if (!docSnap.exists()) {\n          throw new Error('Profile not found');\n        }\n\n        let profileData = docSnap.data() as CrewProfile;\n        // Fallback: use photoURL if profileImageUrl is missing\n        if (!profileData.profileImageUrl \u0026\u0026 profileData.photoURL) {\n          profileData = { ...profileData, profileImageUrl: profileData.photoURL };\n        }\n        console.log('[PublicResumePage] Fetched profile data:', {\n          hasProfileImage: !!profileData.profileImageUrl,\n          profileImageUrl: profileData.profileImageUrl,\n          isBlobUrl: profileData.profileImageUrl?.startsWith('blob:'),\n          profileData: { ...profileData, profileImageUrl: '...' }\n        });\n\n        if (!profileData.isPublished) {\n          throw new Error('Profile is not published');\n        }\n\n        setProfile(profileData);\n        setStatus(LOADING_STATES.SUCCESS);\n      } catch (err) {\n        console.error('Error fetching resume:', err);\n        setError(err instanceof Error ? err.message : 'An unknown error occurred');\n        setStatus(LOADING_STATES.ERROR);\n      }\n    };\n\n    fetchResume();\n  }, [uid]);",

+ /**
+  * Formats an Instagram handle to ensure it always displays with exactly one @ symbol
+  * @param handle - The Instagram handle (with or without @)
+  * @returns Properly formatted Instagram handle with exactly one @ symbol
+  */
+ export function formatInstagramHandle(handle: string): string {
+   if (!handle) return '';
+   
+   // Remove any existing @ symbols and trim whitespace
+   const cleanHandle = handle.replace(/@/g, '').trim();
+   
+   // Return with single @ symbol
+   return cleanHandle ? &#96;@${cleanHandle}&#96; : '';
+ }
+ 
+ /**
+  * Gets the clean Instagram handle without @ symbol for storage
+  * @param handle - The Instagram handle (with or without @)
+  * @returns Clean handle without @ symbol
+  */
+ export function getCleanInstagramHandle(handle: string): string {
+   if (!handle) return '';
+   
+   // Remove any existing @ symbols and trim whitespace
+   return handle.replace(/@/g, '').trim();
+ }

\n            &#96;${profile.residences[0].city}, ${profile.residences[0].country}&#96; : undefined,\n          profileImageUrl: profile.profileImageUrl,\n        });\n        setIsBookmarked(true);\n      }\n    } catch (error) {\n      console.error('Error toggling bookmark:', error);\n    } finally {\n      setBookmarking(false);\n    }\n  };\n\n  const getAvailabilityText = (availability: string) =\u003e {\n    switch (availability.toLowerCase()) {\n      case 'available':\n        return t('crew.available');\n      case 'soon':\n        return t('crew.soon');\n      case 'unavailable':\n        return t('crew.unavailable');\n      default:\n        return availability;\n    }\n  };\n\n  const mainTitle = profile.jobTitles?.[0]?.title || '';\n  const mainLocation = profile.residences?.[0]\n    ?         "contents": "    .skills-section {\n      background: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.05);\n      border: 1px solid rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.1);\n      border-radius: 16px;\n      padding: 24px;\n\n      h3 {\n        font-size: 20px;\n        font-weight: 600;\n        margin: 0 0 16px 0;\n      }\n\n      .skills-grid {\n        display: flex;\n        flex-wrap: wrap;\n        gap: 8px;\n        margin-bottom: 24px;\n\n        .skill-tag {\n          padding: 6px 12px;\n          background: rgba(102, 126, 234, 0.2);\n          border: 1px solid rgba(102, 126, 234, 0.3);\n          border-radius: 20px;\n          font-size: 12px;\n          color: #667eea;\n          font-weight: 500;\n        }\n      }\n\n      .education-list {\n        list-style: none;\n        padding: 0;\n        margin: 0;\n\n        li {\n          padding: 8px 0;\n          border-bottom: 1px solid rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.1);\n\n          \u0026:last-child {\n            border-bottom: none;\n          }\n        }\n      }\n    }\n\n    .contact-section {\n      background: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.05);\n      border: 1px solid rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.1);\n      border-radius: 16px;\n      padding: 24px;\n\n      h3 {\n        font-size: 20px;\n        font-weight: 600;\n        margin: 0 0 20px 0;\n      }\n\n      .contact-info {\n        .contact-item {\n          display: flex;\n          align-items: center;\n          gap: 12px;\n          padding: 12px 0;\n          border-bottom: 1px solid rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.1);\n\n          \u0026:last-child {\n            border-bottom: none;\n          }\n\n          .contact-icon {\n            font-size: 18px;\n            width: 24px;\n            text-align: center;\n          }\n\n          a {\n            color: #667eea;\n            text-decoration: none;\n\n            \u0026:hover {\n              text-decoration: underline;\n            }\n          }\n        }\n      }\n    }\n  }\n\n",

Perfect! It looks like I've covered all the necessary places. Let me create a summary of the changes I've made:

## Summary

I've successfully fixed the Instagram handle display issue where double "@" symbols were appearing. Here's what I implemented:

### 1. **Created Utility Functions** (`src/lib/utils.ts`)
- `formatInstagramHandle(handle: string)`: Ensures Instagram handles always display with exactly one "@" symbol
- `getCleanInstagramHandle(handle: string)`: Removes all "@" symbols for clean storage

### 2. **Updated ResumeView Component** (`src/components/ResumeView.tsx`)
- Added import for `formatInstagramHandle` utility function
- Updated the Instagram display line to use the formatting function instead of hardcoded "@" symbol
- Now displays: `📷 {formatInstagramHandle(profile.contactInfo.instagram)}` instead of `📷 @{profile.contactInfo.instagram}`

### 3. **Updated EditCrewProfile Component** (`src/components/EditCrewProfile.tsx`)
- Added import for `getCleanInstagramHandle` utility function
- Updated the save function to clean Instagram handles before storing them in the database
- Changed the input placeholder to "yourusername (without @)" to guide users

### 4. **How It Works**
- **Input**: Users can enter Instagram handles with or without "@" symbols (e.g., "franciscovaldez", "@franciscovaldez", or "@@franciscovaldez")
- **Storage**: The system automatically removes all "@" symbols and stores clean handles (e.g., "franciscovaldez")
- **Display**: The system automatically adds exactly one "@" symbol when displaying (e.g., "@franciscovaldez")

### 5. **Test Results**
The utility functions handle all edge cases correctly:
- `"franciscovaldez"` → `"@franciscovaldez"`
- `"@franciscovaldez"` → `"@franciscovaldez"`
- `"@@franciscovaldez"` → `"@franciscovaldez"`
- `"  @franciscovaldez  "` → `"@franciscovaldez"`
- Empty/null values → `""`

This solution ensures that Instagram handles are always displayed consistently with exactly one "@" symbol, regardless of how users input them, eliminating the double "@" issue you reported.

+ // Test Instagram handle formatting with existing data
+ const formatInstagramHandle = (handle) =&gt; {
+   if (!handle) return '';
+   
+   // Remove any existing @ symbols and trim whitespace
+   const cleanHandle = handle.replace(/@/g, '').trim();
+   
+   // Return with single @ symbol
+   return cleanHandle ? &#96;@${cleanHandle}&#96; : '';
+ };

## Summary

You're absolutely correct! The fix I implemented works at the **fetch/display level**, which means it will be **retroactive** for all existing users. Here's how it works:

### ✅ **Retroactive Fix for Existing Users**

The `formatInstagramHandle` function in `src/lib/utils.ts` handles **all existing data** correctly:

- **Existing user with "@franciscovaldez"** → Displays as **"@franciscovaldez"** ✅
- **Existing user with "@@franciscovaldez"** → Displays as **"@franciscovaldez"** ✅  
- **Existing user with "franciscovaldez"** → Displays as **"@franciscovaldez"** ✅

### �� **How It Works**

1. **Display Level**: The `formatInstagramHandle` function removes ALL existing "@" symbols and adds exactly one
2. **Storage Level**: New submissions are cleaned before saving (removes all "@" symbols)
3. **Backward Compatible**: Works with all existing data formats

### 📍 **Where It's Applied**

- **ResumeView Component**: The main place where Instagram handles are displayed
- **EditCrewProfile Component**: New submissions are cleaned before saving

### �� **Result**

- **No manual database changes needed**
- **All existing users will see correct formatting immediately**
- **New users will have clean data stored**
- **Consistent display across the entire application**

The fix is now live and will automatically correct the display for all existing users who have Instagram handles stored with "@" symbols, without requiring any manual database updates!

## What's Now Live

The Instagram handle fix is now live on **https://myfilmjobs.com** and will:

- **Fix existing users** with double "@@" symbols (like "@@franciscovaldez" → "@franciscovaldez")
- **Handle new submissions** correctly (stores clean data, displays with single "@")

## Technical Details

The fix includes:
- **Utility functions** in `src/lib/utils.ts` for consistent Instagram handle formatting
- **Updated ResumeView component** to use the formatting function
- **Updated EditCrewProfile component** to clean data before saving
- **Backward compatibility** for all existing data formats

Your users will now see correctly formatted Instagram handles across the entire application! 🎉

## Summary

The fix has been successfully deployed, but there's a **CDN caching issue**. Here's what's happening:

### ✅ **Fix is Deployed Successfully**
- The code changes are in the build
- The deployment was successful
- The preview channel shows fresh content

### ⏰ **CDN Cache Issue**
- The main site has `x-cache: HIT` (serving cached content)
- Cache-control is set to 1 hour (`max-age=3600`)
- The CDN is serving the old cached version

### 🔧 **Solutions**

**Option 1: Wait for cache to expire (1 hour)**
- The cache will automatically expire in about 1 hour
- Then the new version will be served

**Option 2: Test the preview URL now**
- You can test the fix immediately at: `https://myfilmjobs-com--preview-a0hzdqyo.web.app`
- This URL has the latest code without caching

**Option 3: Force cache refresh**
- Try accessing the site with a hard refresh (Ctrl+Shift+R or Cmd+Shift+R)
- Or try incognito/private browsing mode

The fix is definitely deployed and working - it's just a matter of waiting for the CDN cache to expire or using the preview URL to test immediately!
